biography: Stefano Modena, born under the scorching Italian sun, practically came out of the womb with a steering wheel in his hands. His father, a mechanic with grease permanently etched under his fingernails, introduced him to the intoxicating scent of gasoline before he could even walk. Stefano started tearing around the local karting tracks at age 10, his raw talent immediately apparent. He famously elbowed his way to victory in his first national karting championship, a move that earned him both accolades and a reputation. Climbing the ranks swiftly, he landed a seat with EuroUno Racing, a team known for nurturing young talent. His aggressive style and relentless pursuit of victory quickly made him a fan favorite, even if it occasionally ruffled feathers within the paddock. Currently, at the peak of his career with Paddy G.P., he's a force to be reckoned with, a fiery competitor constantly pushing the limits of both himself and his machine.
drivingStyle: Modena's driving style is a visceral, unapologetic expression of aggression. He attacks corners with a ferocity that borders on reckless, often pushing the car right to the edge of adhesion. Tire management isn't his strongest suit; he prefers to extract every last ounce of performance early on, knowing he can compensate later with sheer speed. Under pressure, he becomes even more formidable, transforming into a relentless predator who won't hesitate to exploit any weakness in his opponents. His 'never lift' attitude has earned him both wins and DNFs, but it's undeniably what makes him such an exciting driver to watch.

rivalries.reason: A long-standing feud stemming from a controversial collision at the Monza Grand Prix. Both drivers blame each other.
A clash of styles. Nakamura's smooth, calculated approach is the antithesis of Modena's raw aggression, leading to frequent on-track battles.
Off-track tension. Rossi and Modena are known for their heated exchanges in press conferences, fueled by constant one-upmanship.

quirks: Always wears the same worn-out leather driving gloves, claiming they bring him luck.
Listens to opera at full volume in his motorhome before every race to 'channel his inner Italian spirit'.
Refuses to eat anything green on race day, believing it jinxes his chances.
famousQuote: "Second place is just the first loser."
careerHighlight: Winning the Monaco Grand Prix after starting from 10th on the grid, overtaking three cars in the final lap with a daring display of skill and bravery.
careerLowPoint: Crashing out of the Italian Grand Prix on the final lap while leading, handing the victory to his arch-rival, Jean-Pierre Dubois.
